title: Single-cell foundation models: a review that narrows its own objections
author: Codex conversation; exact model identifier not recorded
workflow: MAR skill evidence challenge and synthesis
summary: The review identifies three revision priorities, two verification questions, one supported strength and four dismissed concerns. The priorities concern the scope of the model comparison, the interpretation of pretraining size, and the metric description. Each assessment below separates the reported evidence from its interpretation.
coverage: Read: abstract, article body, methods, figure captions, availability statements and supplement descriptions from the published April 2025 article. The actual offline CLI produced 32 leads from 80 source blocks. The scientific synthesis is one model-native review using multiple lenses, not six independent reviewers. Supplement files, figure images, raw data, code execution and published peer-review history were not inspected. Thus neither numerical results nor supplementary sensitivity analyses are independently verified.

items.title: Scope of the model comparison
items.assessment: The study compares frozen foundation models with scVI and Harmony fitted to the evaluation data using batch labels. This estimates practical performance under different fitting conditions; it does not isolate architecture or pretraining quality.
items.challenge: The authors explain these differences in terms of available computing resources and limit their conclusions to selected models and tasks. The review therefore narrows the concern to how the comparison is interpreted.
items.next_step: List target-data fitting, batch-label access, feature selection and computing budget for each method. A claim about architecture alone would require a comparison with matched information and adaptation; the practical benchmark does not require that additional analysis.
items.decision_change: Close this as a presentation check if all conclusions already describe performance under the tested conditions.

items.title: Pretraining size and tissue composition
items.assessment: Performance does not increase consistently across the tested model versions. Because pretraining size and tissue composition change together, this result does not identify a general limit beyond which more training data stops improving performance.
items.challenge: The paper acknowledges this confounding and states that the larger human collection includes the smaller tissue collections. The remaining concern is the scope of the scaling conclusion.
items.next_step: Describe the performance of the tested variants without inferring a data-volume limit. A later scaling study would need to hold tissue mixture, training procedure and evaluation datasets fixed while varying pretraining size and random seeds; this may require new model training.
items.decision_change: A controlled scaling experiment showing the same plateau would support a stronger claim. Narrow wording alone resolves the current interpretation concern.

items.title: Direction of the ASW metric
items.assessment: The biological-preservation paragraph describes normalized zero as strong within-cluster cohesion, then states that higher average silhouette width (ASW) indicates better separation. These descriptions need reconciliation before readers can interpret the rankings.
items.challenge: The paragraph states the intended higher-is-better direction. A wording error could leave the computed results unchanged.
items.next_step: Check the scib transformation and the negative, zero and positive raw-silhouette cases against the archived code. Correct the description to match the implementation; determine whether recomputation is needed only after that check.
items.decision_change: An explicitly documented alternative normalization consistent with both prose and implementation would remove the concern; a prose-only correction should not be treated as changed scientific results.

items.title: Masked reconstruction sensitivity
items.assessment: The reconstruction diagnostic supplies unmasked input, whereas pretraining uses corrupted input. Performance on the diagnostic alone does not establish whether a model learned its training objective.
items.challenge: The supplement description reports Geneformer results across masking fractions. Those figures were not inspected, so the adequacy of that sensitivity analysis remains unverified.
items.next_step: Inspect Supplementary Figures S8–S9 and the code for the masking ratio, scored tokens and information available to the simple comparator. If these do not address the question, evaluate matched masking and scoring conditions for each model and dataset, with uncertainty across repeated masks.
items.decision_change: Equivalent conclusions under the training-like corruption and scoring protocol would substantially weaken this concern.

items.title: Baselines and reported evaluation scope
items.assessment: The study includes simple baselines, a randomly initialized model, and tests of cell separation and batch integration. These comparisons provide context for interpreting the performance of pretrained models.
items.challenge: The authors limit coverage to selected models and tasks. The reported comparisons do not independently verify the numerical results or establish performance of later model versions.
items.next_step: Retain these comparisons and the stated scope; report results for each dataset alongside aggregate rankings.
items.decision_change: A code or data audit finding materially different computations could change this assessment; none was performed here.

items.title: Code-availability statements refer to different studies
items.assessment: The engine combined a statement about other methods lacking public pretraining code with this paper’s code-release statement. The statements refer to different studies and do not contradict each other.
items.challenge: The paper explicitly provides its own analysis repository and archived software environment.
items.next_step: Close the contradiction lead. Repository accessibility and executable reproduction remain separate checks.
items.decision_change: Evidence that the cited release lacks the actual analyses would justify a new, more specific reproducibility concern.

items.title: Pretraining overlap is disclosed
items.assessment: The paper discloses pretraining overlap and describes a Pancreas analysis without overlap. The evidence does not support a concern about undisclosed overlap or absent sensitivity analysis.
items.challenge: The authors acknowledge that some scGPT batch-integration advantages cannot be separated from prior exposure. Disclosure does not establish performance on unseen data for every comparison.
items.next_step: Retain the exposure limitation and inspect the supplementary results for each dataset before assessing generalization.
items.decision_change: A headline asserting uniformly unseen evaluation, or a mismatch between the reported subset and actual inputs, would reopen a narrower concern.

items.title: Perturbation-screen checks are outside the study scope
items.assessment: The study evaluates pretrained embeddings and reconstruction. It does not report a new CRISPR screen, so screen-specific control requirements do not apply to this benchmark. Donor-level differential-expression checks also require an applicable inferential analysis.
items.challenge: The experimental-validation passage proposes future research.
items.next_step: Mark these leads out of scope. Apply experiment-specific checks if a later manuscript reports those experiments.
items.decision_change: A newly supplied experimental screen or inferential differential-expression analysis would change applicability.

items.title: Methods details requiring supplementary material
items.assessment: The supplement descriptions identify additional sampling and evaluation details. Donor composition, preprocessing, random seeds, uncertainty and robustness require inspection of those materials and the archived code; a text-search omission does not establish a missing method.
items.challenge: Subsampling is described and an executable environment is announced. Neither was checked here.
items.next_step: Inspect Tables S1–S7 and the archived environment. Record donor and dataset units, random seeds, and whether resampling measures donor or only cell variability. Raise a concern only if a requirement relevant to the stated conclusion remains unmet.
items.decision_change: Locating the relevant settings or showing that an inferential claim is not made closes the corresponding lead; reproducibility failure would warrant a specific issue.

items.title: Baseline comparisons are reported
items.assessment: The paper includes highly variable gene (HVG), scVI and Harmony baselines, plus a randomly initialized scGPT comparison. The generic missing-baseline lead is unsupported.
items.challenge: Differences in fitting conditions remain a separate interpretation question in SC-1.
items.next_step: Close the missing-baseline and absent-random-control leads. Justify any additional comparator against the specific claim it would test.
items.decision_change: A necessary comparator for a stronger, different claim could reopen a narrowly specified request.

baseline_triage.reason: Different subjects were conflated in the code-availability check.
Comparators and a random-initialization control are described.
Pretraining overlap and the remaining exposure limitation are disclosed.
Batch information differs across approaches and is explicitly discussed.
No new CRISPR screen, differential-expression inference or deployed clinical classifier is evaluated here.

baseline_triage.decision: Verify in unreviewed materials or establish applicability
baseline_triage.reason: Inspect supplement/code before treating these reporting cues as study defects; several are optional for a descriptive benchmark.

assessment.text: The benchmark compares frozen single-cell models with methods fitted to the evaluation data. This design assesses practical performance; it does not isolate the effects of architecture or pretraining size.

contribution.text: Includes simple baselines and a randomly initialized model, with tests of cell separation and batch integration.

priorities.text: State which methods use evaluation data for fitting and which use batch labels when interpreting performance differences.
Limit the scaling conclusion to the tested models: pretraining size and tissue composition vary together.
Check the average silhouette width (ASW) description against the implemented normalization.

first_step.text: Revise the comparison and scaling conclusions to match the stated design limits. These wording changes do not require new experiments.

at_a_glance.scope: Published April 2025 article. Offline CLI plus model-native synthesis; text, methods and captions reviewed. Supplements, code and results were not independently checked; no independent human validation of this review.
